title: Netflix's 'Best of the Best' Puts South Asian Dance Culture Center Stage
excerpt: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan and Priyanka Kedia lead the Hasan Minhaj-penned Bollywood-fusion dance comedy, arriving on Netflix on September 18.
body:
• Netflix has unveiled the first look of Best of the Best, a coming-of-age comedy set in the world of competitive collegiate Bollywood-fusion dance at UCLA
  • The film stars Never Have I Ever's Maitreyi Ramakrishnan and Priyanka Kedia as childhood best friends navigating friendship and fierce competition on the road to the U.S. Championship
  • Co-written by Hasan Minhaj and Prashanth Venkataramanujam, the film features an ensemble cast including Lilly Singh, Ankur Rathee, and Janina Gavankar
  • Directed by Lena Khan, who previously helmed several episodes of Never Have I Ever, the film debuts globally on Netflix on September 18, 2026

First Look Unveiled

Netflix has released the first look at Best of the Best, a coming-of-age dance comedy that dives into the high-stakes world of collegiate Bollywood-fusion dance competitions. The film follows Maya and Anjali, two childhood best friends who join UCLA's competitive dance team and discover that the road to winning the U.S. Championship is far more cutthroat than they imagined.

The project, which was originally developed at Amazon MGM under the title For The Culture before moving to Netflix, filmed in New Jersey between July 28 and September 11, 2025. It is set for a global premiere on Netflix on September 18, 2026.

A Stacked South Asian Cast

Maitreyi Ramakrishnan, the 24-year-old Tamil-Canadian actress who broke out as Devi Vishkumar in Mindy Kaling's Never Have I Ever, returns to Netflix in her first on-screen role for the streamer since that series ended in 2023. Since then, she has appeared in Freakier Friday, voiced a role in the animated film The Twits, and joined the fifth season of The Boys in a guest role as Countess Crow. She plays Maya.

Priyanka Kedia, whose credits include the film Everything to Me and short films Pleats and Color My Grey Street, plays Anjali. The ensemble also includes Ankur Rathee (Single Papa), Janina Gavankar (The Morning Show), Chaneil Kular (Sex Education), Shreya Navile (Month of Madhu), and Becky Alex, along with Lilly Singh, Nihar Duvvuri, Nico Greetham, Amryn Khurana, Tanishq Joshi, Saara Chaudry, and Sasha Bhasin (XO, Kitty).

"This story celebrates the vibrancy of Bollywood Fusion dance, the growing pains of young adulthood, and the lasting power of true friendship."

— Netflix, official synopsis

Minhaj and Khan Reunite Behind the Camera

Hasan Minhaj, best known for Patriot Act with Hasan Minhaj on Netflix and roles in It Ends with Us and Haunted Mansion, co-wrote the screenplay with Prashanth Venkataramanujam. Both also serve as producers through their production company, 186K Films. Jonathan Eirich produces through Rideback, with Netflix's head of film Dan Lin also involved. Ellen H. Schwartz and Ryan Halprin serve as executive producers.

Director Lena Khan previously helmed the 2021 Disney+ film Flora & Ulysses and directed several episodes of Never Have I Ever, making her a natural fit for a story rooted in South Asian identity and youth culture.

Why Bollywood Dance Competitions Matter

On college campuses across the United States, competitive Bollywood-fusion dance teams have emerged as some of the most vibrant spaces for South Asian community building and cultural connection. Teams from universities nationwide — including UCLA, UC Berkeley, Stanford, and the University of Michigan — compete in circuits like Bollywood America and Legends, drawing thousands of spectators and millions of online views.

These competitions blend classical Indian dance forms with hip-hop, contemporary, and Bollywood choreography, creating a genre that is distinctly diasporic. For many second-generation South Asian Americans, dance teams are where cultural identity is performed, debated, and celebrated. Best of the Best is the first major studio production to place this world at the center of its narrative.

The Diaspora Connection

The film arrives at a moment when South Asian representation in Hollywood continues to expand beyond token roles. Ramakrishnan's career trajectory — from a breakout Netflix debut to major studio films — mirrors the broader shift. With Minhaj behind the screenplay and a cast that includes multiple actors of South Asian descent, the film is positioned as a cultural event for the Indian and South Asian diaspora.

What's Next

Ramakrishnan has a packed slate beyond Best of the Best. She will voice a character in The Angry Birds Movie 3, due for theatrical release in December 2026, and has been cast in a recurring role in the second season of Prime Video's Elle, a Legally Blonde prequel series. She is also attached to Netflix's The Netherfield Girls, a contemporary adaptation of Pride and Prejudice.

Best of the Best streams globally on Netflix from September 18, 2026.
